lines.text: F. 412. Περὶ δραπετῶν Νικαέως Πρωταγόρου 1.
lines.en: F. 412. On runaways, by Protagoras of Nicaea 1.

lines.text: Ἐὰν εὑρεθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης τοῦ ὡροσκόπου τῆς φυγῆς ἀναπο-
lines.en: If the ruler of the ascendant of the flight is found retro-

lines.text: δίζων, ὁ φυγὼν αὐτομάτως ἐπανελεύσεται πρὸς τὸν δεσπότην· ἐὰν δὲ
lines.en: grading, the runaway will return of his own accord to the master; but if

lines.text: ἐν ἰδίῳ οἴκῳ εὑρεθῇ ἢ ὁρίοις καὶ μὴ ἀναποδίζων, ὁ ἀποδρὰς ἔνδον τῶν
lines.en: he is found in his own house or terms and not retrograding, the runaway will be found inside the

lines.text: οἰκιῶν ἢ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἢ ἐν τῇ περιχώρῳ εὑρεθήσεται· καὶ θᾶττον ἐὰν ἐν
lines.en: houses or in the city or in the surrounding area; and faster if in

lines.text: τῷ ὑπεργείῳ ἡμισφαιρίῳ τύχῃ, ὥσπερ οὖν βραδύτερον εἰ ἐν τῷ ὑπὸ
lines.en: the hemisphere above the earth he happens to be, just as slower if in the one under

lines.text: γῆν. τῆς Σελήνης οὔσης ἐν τῷ μεσουρανήματι, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἐν τῷ δεξιῷ
lines.en: the earth. The Moon being in the midheaven, that is in the right

lines.text: τετραγώνῳ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου, διὰ τῶν δεξιῶν μερῶν τῆς οἰκίας, ἀφ’ ἧς
lines.en: square of the ascendant, through the right parts of the house, from which

lines.text: ὁ δραπέτης ἤρξατο τῆς φυγῆς, τὴν πάροδον πεποίηται· ἐν δὲ τῷ
lines.en: the runaway began the flight, he has made the passage; but in the

lines.text: εὐωνύμῳ τετραγώνῳ ὁμοίως διὰ τῶν ἀριστερῶν μερῶν· ὁ γὰρ ὡρο-
lines.en: left square similarly through the left parts; for the as-

lines.text: σκόπος ἀντὶ τῶν πυλῶν τῆς οἰκίας νοεῖται. ἡ δὲ Σελήνη βορρᾶν
lines.en: cendant is understood instead of the gates of the house. And the Moon going north

lines.text: κατερχομένη μηνύει τὸν φυγόντα κατὰ μεσημβρίαν πεπορεῦσθαι καὶ
lines.en: indicates the runaway has travelled towards the south and

lines.text: εὑρεθήσεσθαι ἐν ἡμέραις κεʹ· νότον δὲ ἡ Σελήνη κατιοῦσα, ἐν τοῖς κατὰ
lines.en: will be found in 25 days; but the Moon going down south, in the places towards

lines.text: δύσιν τόποις ἐν ἡμέραις μβʹ εὑρεθήσεσθαι, ἐν καθύγροις τόποις καὶ
lines.en: the west in 42 days will be found, in very wet places and

lines.text: ἀνημέροις ἢ δυσχειμέροις· νότον δὲ ἀνιοῦσα, ἐν τοῖς ἀνατολικοῖς τόποις
lines.en: wild or wintry; but going up south, in the eastern places

lines.text: καὶ δυσκόλως μηνυθήσεσθαι ἐν ἡμέραις ξδʹ· βορρᾶν δὲ ἀνερχομένη, ἐν
lines.en: and with difficulty will be indicated in 64 days; but going up north, in

lines.text: τοῖς ἀρκτικοῖς τόποις καὶ δυσκόλως εὑρεθήσεσθαι μηνύει.
lines.en: the northern places and with difficulty will be found, it indicates.

lines.text: Ἐκ τῆς τῶν ζῳδίων δὲ φύσεως καταστοχαστέον τὸν τόπον. εἰς
lines.en: From the nature of the zodiac signs one must guess the place. Into

lines.text: [f. 412v] ὃν ἀπελεύσεται ὁ φυγών, οἷον εἰ μὲν Κριός, νομαίους καὶ πεδι-
lines.en: [f. 412v] which the runaway will depart, for example if Aries, pastoral and plain-

lines.text: νούς· εἰ δὲ Ταῦρος, ἐπιπέδους καὶ πεπονημένους· εἰ δὲ Δίδυμοι...
lines.en: like; but if Taurus, flat and worked; but if Gemini...

sections.text:
1 Excerptum, cuius initium cum hoc fragmento Neapolitano conspirat,
invenitur in cod. Veneto 6, f. 123, ροζʹ, eodem titulo. In Parisino autem 2506,
saec. XIII, f. 36 praemittitur rubrica : Περὶ δραπετῶν ἔγραψεν ὁ Δωρόθεος ἐν τῷ
ἄλλῳ βιβλίῳ· ὧδε λέγομεν τὰ τοῦ Νικαέως Πρωταγόρου. Nec dubium est, quin
scriptor byzantinus, qui Syntagma Parisinum congessit, haec omnia ex ultimo
capite (37) lib. III Hephaestionis adhuc inedito hauserit ; cf. Kroll, Philolo-
gus, LVII, 4; Engelbrecht, Hephästion von Theben, p. 36. — Πρωταγόρου συνα-
γωγαί una cum libris Hermetis et Petosiridis laudantur in fragmento edito Catal.
Flor., p. 126, 6, et item excerptum ἐκ τῶν συναγωγῶν Πρωταγόρου traditur in
cod. Vatic. 1056, saec. XIV, f. 79. Aetas scriptoris incerta est, nisi forte Protagoras
hic Nicaeensis idem sit atque Πρωταγόρας ἀστρολόγος, in quem Euphorion
(natus 276 a. C.) epicedion composuit teste Laertio Diogene, IX, 56 [F. C. qui cod.
Paris. contulit].
sections.en: 1 An excerpt, whose beginning agrees with this Neapolitan fragment, is found in cod. Venetus 6, f. 123, 177, with the same title. In Parisinus 2506, however, 13th cent., f. 36, a rubric is prefixed: 'Dorotheus wrote about runaways in the other book; here we say the things of Protagoras of Nicaea'. Nor is there any doubt that the Byzantine writer, who compiled the Syntagma Parisinum, drew all these things from the last chapter (37) of book III of Hephaestion, still unpublished; cf. Kroll, Philologus, LVII, 4; Engelbrecht, Hephästion von Theben, p. 36. — The Collections of Protagoras together with the books of Hermes and Petosiris are praised in the fragment edited in Catal. Flor., p. 126, 6, and likewise an excerpt 'from the collections of Protagoras' is transmitted in cod. Vatic. 1056, 14th cent., f. 79. The age of the writer is uncertain, unless perhaps this Protagoras of Nicaea is the same as 'Protagoras the astrologer', upon whom Euphorion (born 276 B.C.) composed an epicedion according to the testimony of Diogenes Laertius, IX, 56 [F. C. who collated the Paris codex].

summary.headline: Protagoras on Runaways
summary.text: Protagoras of Nicaea’s astrological rules for locating runaways, using the ascendant ruler, retrogradation, houses, terms, the Moon’s direction and position, and zodiac-sign qualities to predict direction, terrain, and time of discovery.
